arxiv-2504-06271.title: ER-RAG: Enhance RAG with ER-Based Unified Modeling of Heterogeneous Data Sources Thanks: ∗ Equal Contribution. † Corresponding Authors.
arxiv-2504-06271.creator: Yikuan Xia ∗1 , Jiazun Chen ∗1 , Yirui Zhan 1 , Suifeng Zhao 1 , Weipeng Jiang 2 , Chaorui Zhang 2 , Wei Han 2 , Bo Bai †2 , Jun Gao †1
arxiv-2504-06271.description: Abstract . Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated significant potential in performing question-answering (QA) tasks. Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) enhances the reliability and precision of LLMs through the integration of external evidence beyond their training data. The supporting evidence is retrieved from external sources, including web pages, databases, and knowledge graphs, among other structured and unstructured data sources.

arxiv-2512-20502.title: Viscoelastic Material Properties of Gelatin with Varying Water to Collagen Mass Ratios
arxiv-2512-20502.creator: J. E. Bonavia \affilnum 1
arxiv-2512-20502.description: Abstract Gelatin is often used as an analog for studying soft and biological materials in order to understand the mechanics of behavior of biological tissue in events like traumatic brain injuries. The material properties of gelatin change with the ratio of water to gelatin powder used to make a given sample.

pmc-12538959.creator: Kate Fryer, Josie Reynolds, Qizhi Huang, Rebecca Mawson, Emma Linton, Habiba Aminu, Johanna White, Ryan Cory, Caroline Mitchell, University of Sheffield, Leeds University, Sheffield Chinese Community Centre, Sheffield African Caribbean Mental Health Association, Shipshape, Children and Young People’
pmc-12538959.description: BackgroundPeople from ethnic minority and socioeconomically deprived backgrounds remain underrepresented in primary healthcare research despite experiencing worse health outcomes and healthcare experiences. Traditional engagement approaches often maintain power imbalances by keeping control within academic institutions, failing to achieve meaningful representation or change.

pmc-12587500.title: TelOMpy enables single-molecule resolution of telomere length from optical genome mapping data
pmc-12587500.creator: Ivan Pokrovac, Sunčica Stipoljev, Željka Pezer
pmc-12587500.description: BackgroundExisting methods for assessing telomere length suffer from various limitations, including low resolution, narrow scope, limited throughput, and poor reproducibility. These issues largely arise from the reliance on laborious and indirect approaches to telomere length measurement.ResultsWe developed TelOMpy, a bioinformatics tool designed to determine the lengths of individual telomeres from optical genome mapping data.

pmc-12622571.title: Ventral Attention Network Resting State Functional Connectivity: Psychosocial Correlates among US Adolescents
pmc-12622571.creator: Shervin Assari, Alexandra Donovan, Babak Najand, Golnoush Akhlaghipour, Mario F Mendez
pmc-12622571.description: Background:Resting-state functional MRI (rsfMRI) provides insights into large-scale brain network organization associated with cognitive control, emotion regulation, and attentional processes. The ventral attention network (VAN) is a key salience-driven network that supports attentional re-orienting to behaviorally relevant stimuli. However, little is known about how VAN resting state functional connectivity varies by demographic, socioeconomic, psychosocial, and behavioral factors during early adolescence.

pmc-12629417.title: Reinforcing intensive motherhood: A study of gender bias in parental responsibilities allocation by large language models
pmc-12629417.creator: Jiaxing Xiu, Yongjie Sun, Zheng Zhang, Zheng Zhang, Zheng Zhang
pmc-12629417.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). This study investigated gender bias in Large Language Models (LLMs) within the context of parenting responsibility attribution, focusing on whether LLMs implicitly reinforce the ideology of “intensive mothering” by assigning caregiving duties predominantly to mothers. pmc-13143545.title: Complications of Pregnancy and Birth in Women With Vascular Malformations: A Nationwide Cross‐Sectional Study
pmc-13143545.creator: Delano J. de Oliveira Marreiros, Max M. Lokhorst, Sophie E. R. Horbach, Merel L. E. Stor, Naomi van Hout, Victor E. A. Gerdes, Wessel Ganzevoort, Chantal M. A. M. van der Horst

pmc-13202028.title: Impacts of national volume-based procurement policy on insulin price, volume and expenditure in China: a quasi-experimental study
pmc-13202028.creator: Hongbin Yi, Shuhua Tan, Mengtian Cai, Liping Kuai, Dongyan Xu, Sheng Han
pmc-13202028.description: IntroductionTo alleviate the diabetes economic burden, the Chinese government implemented the national volume-based procurement (NVBP) policy exclusively for insulin in May 2022. However, there is limited evidence on the impact of NVBP policy on insulin procurement prices, volumes and expenditures.MethodsWe conducted an interrupted time series analysis (ITSA) to evaluate the policy’s impacts on insulin procurement prices, volumes and expenditure.

pmc-13365958.title: IFPHOR0096 Students as Changemakers: Fostering Interdisciplinary Engagement in Sustainable Healthcare
pmc-13365958.creator: Harshini Suresh, Ashley Thian, Lana Kaedbey
pmc-13365958.description: Understanding the relationship between planetary health and human health is pivotal for the long-term sustainability of our healthcare systems. An audit of the Planetary Health Report Card (2025) revealed low levels of student engagement in sustainability in healthcare, despite discourse within public health.A student-led, cross-faculty conference aimed to encourage interdisciplinary collaboration in sustainability.
